prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1300; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a sideswipe while changing lanes and said the other vehicle drifted into the adjacent lane as they moved over. The claimant reports a wrist fracture from the event and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the initial statement from the claimant, which described the lane change and contact on the driver's side. The account has stayed consistent across each conversation so far.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the vehicles made contact during the merge and described the same sequence of movements. Their account lines up with what the claimant has said.

Entry 4: Police report notes that the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene, and two witnesses gave statements that match the described impact. Photos from the scene were added to the file.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle and the damage pattern on the driver's side fits the impact described by all parties. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior records or the claimant's disclosures.

Entry 6: Confirmed the policy coverage start date and found nothing indicating the damage predates it. The driver of the vehicle lives with the policyholder and is listed as a household member under the policy.

Entry 7: Obtained initial medical records showing a wrist fracture. Whether this injury stems from the collision has not yet been determined, and additional records are needed before a causation view can be formed.

Entry 8: Claimant's provider notes no prior injury to the same wrist or arm, and the claimant has not mentioned any earlier problems with that area during any contact.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of fracture. Requested updated treatment notes and follow-up imaging to understand the recovery timeline.

Entry 10: Spoke with the claimant again by phone. The claimant repeated the same account of the lane change and the contact, with no changes in sequence or detail from earlier conversations.

Entry 11: Reviewed the photos and witness statements together and they support the reported impact and the vehicle damage. Nothing in the file currently points to a different sequence of events.

Entry 12: Open items remain the medical causation review and the updated treatment records. Will follow up with the treating provider and reassess once those documents are received.
